nodes.name: Defining DP states and transitions
nodes.description: Express the answer for a state (an index, a remaining capacity, the last choice) through smaller states; say what each state means and fix the base cases before coding.

facets.recognize: Spots overlapping subproblems and choices whose effects carry forward (count ways, min/max cost, feasibility).
facets.explain: States in words what dp[i] or dp[i][j] means and why the transition covers every choice.
facets.implement: Writes the recurrence with correct base cases.

misconceptions.desc: Used a greedy choice where an earlier choice limits later ones (frog jump, coins of arbitrary values).
Left information out of the state (last activity, holding a stock, transactions left), so transitions were wrong.
Wrong or missing base cases (index 0, a negative index, target 0).
Cannot say what a table cell means.

nodes.name: Memoization (top-down)
nodes.description: Cache each state's answer the first time it is computed, so the recursion evaluates every state once.

facets.recognize: Sees when plain recursion revisits the same states, so caching them pays off.
facets.explain: Explains why memoization turns exponential recursion into O(states x transitions).
facets.implement: Checks the cache first, stores before returning and shares one table across calls.

misconceptions.desc: Checked the cache but never stored the computed value.
Used 0 as 'not computed' when 0 is a valid answer, so states were recomputed.
Passed the memo table by value, so cached results were lost.
Did not consider recursion depth for large inputs (stack overflow).

nodes.name: Tabulation (bottom-up)
nodes.description: Fill the table from the base cases toward the answer in an order where every state a cell needs is already filled.

facets.explain: Explains how the fill order follows from the recurrence.
facets.implement: Sizes the table, sets base cases and loops in a valid order.

misconceptions.desc: Filled the table in an order that reads cells not yet computed.
Mixed 0-based and 1-based indices after shifting the table for base cases.
Initialized with 0 where impossible states need infinity (or minus infinity), or the reverse.

nodes.name: Space optimization
nodes.description: When a row depends only on the previous row (or a few previous values), keep just those instead of the full table.

facets.implement: Keeps prev and cur rows (or two variables) and moves cur into prev after each row.
facets.adapt: Uses a single row, iterating capacity backwards for 0/1 and forwards for unbounded choices.

misconceptions.desc: Overwrote values of the previous row that were still needed.
Did not move cur into prev after each row.
Iterated capacity in the wrong direction, turning 0/1 into unbounded (or the reverse).

nodes.name: 1D DP
nodes.description: dp[i] depends on a few earlier values: stairs, frog jumps, non-adjacent sums. A circular array becomes two linear runs.

facets.implement: Writes the recurrence with bounds-checked lookbacks.
facets.adapt: Handles k-step jumps and circular arrays.

misconceptions.desc: For a circular array, did not solve twice (without the first, then without the last element).
With k jumps, read dp[i - j] for i - j < 0.
Allowed picking adjacent elements (added a[i] to dp[i - 1]).

nodes.name: DP on grids
nodes.description: dp[i][j] comes from the cells you can arrive from (above, left, diagonals); obstacles contribute 0 ways or infinite cost.

facets.recognize: Spots path counting and min/max path cost on grids.
facets.implement: Sets the first row and column correctly and handles obstacles.
facets.adapt: Handles triangles, any-start falling paths and two walkers at once (a 3D state).

misconceptions.desc: Initialized the first row or column wrongly (an obstacle blocks every cell after it).
Did not set an obstacle cell to 0 ways or infinite cost.
Read column j - 1 or j + 1 outside the row in falling-path or triangle problems.
With two walkers, counted a shared cell twice.

nodes.name: 0/1 knapsack and subset sums
nodes.description: State (index, remaining capacity or target): take the item if it fits, or skip it; each item is used at most once.

facets.recognize: Maps partition, subset-sum, target-sum and difference questions onto 0/1 knapsack.
facets.explain: Explains why the state needs both the index and the remaining target.
facets.implement: Writes take / not-take with dp[i - 1] for both branches.
facets.adapt: Counts subsets correctly with zeros, reads the minimum difference from the last row and turns a difference into a target.

misconceptions.desc: When counting subsets, the base case ignored zeros (with a[0] == 0 there are two ways to make sum 0).
For the minimum difference, did not scan every reachable sum in the last row up to total / 2.
For partitions with difference d, did not reduce to target (total - d) / 2, or did not reject odd or negative total - d.
Let an item be reused (read dp[i] instead of dp[i - 1] after taking it).
Used plain recursion (2^n) without memoizing on (index, target).

nodes.name: Unbounded knapsack
nodes.description: Like 0/1 knapsack, but taking an item stays at the same index so it can be taken again (coins, rod pieces).

facets.explain: Explains why staying at index i allows reuse, and why greedy fails for general coin sets.
facets.implement: Writes the take branch at the same index, with a safe 'impossible' value.

misconceptions.desc: Moved to i - 1 after taking an item, which forbids reuse.
Added 1 to an INT_MAX 'impossible' value and overflowed, or returned it instead of -1.
Took the largest coin first; greedy fails for general coin sets.
Counted orderings instead of combinations (looped amounts outside coins).

nodes.name: DP on two strings
nodes.description: State (i, j) = prefixes of both strings: matching characters move diagonally, otherwise take the best of skipping one side.

facets.recognize: Maps LCS, edit distance, matching and palindromic subsequences onto a two-index table.
facets.explain: Explains each transition in terms of the last characters.
facets.implement: Writes the shifted table with base row and column.
facets.adapt: Prints the LCS, handles substrings, supersequences, edit operations and wildcard matching.

misconceptions.desc: Treated a common substring like a subsequence (did not reset to 0 on a mismatch).
Compared s[i] with t[j] in a table shifted by one (should be s[i - 1] and t[j - 1]).
When printing, walked back the wrong way on a match or a tie.
Left out one of insert, delete or replace in edit distance.
Treated * as one character, or did not let a run of * match an empty prefix.
Counted distinct subsequences in int or without the modulus, overflowing.

nodes.name: Stock problems as state machines
nodes.description: State (day, holding or not, transactions left): each day buy, sell or rest. Cooldown skips a day after selling; a fee is paid per transaction.

facets.recognize: Maps every buy/sell variant onto the same state machine.
facets.implement: Writes buy and sell transitions with the transaction count changing once per transaction.
facets.adapt: Adds a cooldown day, a fee or a limit of k transactions.

misconceptions.desc: Used the one-transaction trick (track the minimum) for problems allowing several transactions.
Counted a transaction on both buy and sell, halving the allowed number.
After selling, allowed buying the next day despite the cooldown.
For unlimited transactions, missed that summing every positive day-to-day gain is enough.

nodes.name: Longest increasing subsequence
nodes.description: dp[i] = 1 + the best dp[j] with j < i and a[j] < a[i] (O(n²), with a parent array to print); patience sorting with lower bound gives the length in O(n log n).

facets.recognize: Maps chains, nesting and divisibility questions onto LIS after sorting.
facets.explain: Explains what the O(n log n) tails array holds and why it is not the LIS itself.
facets.implement: Takes the maximum over all dp[i] and uses lower bound for strictly increasing.
facets.adapt: Prints the LIS, handles bitonic sequences and counts the number of LIS.

misconceptions.desc: Believes the O(n log n) tails array is itself an increasing subsequence of the input.
Used upper_bound where lower_bound was needed for strictly increasing (or the reverse).
Returned dp[n - 1] instead of the maximum over all dp[i].
For divisible subsets or string chains, did not sort first.
When counting LIS, did not reset the count on a longer length and add on an equal one.

nodes.name: Partition (interval) DP
nodes.description: State (i, j) is a range: try every split point k, combine both sides plus the cost of the split, filling by increasing range length.

facets.recognize: Spots 'best way to split or order operations on a range' problems.
facets.explain: Explains why the two sides of a split are independent.
facets.implement: Fills by increasing length (or i descending) with the right split cost.
facets.adapt: Handles cutting sticks, bursting balloons, boolean expressions and front partitions.

misconceptions.desc: Filled by i and j directly instead of by increasing length (or i descending).
In burst balloons, chose the first balloon to burst instead of the last, so the sides were not independent.
Did not sort the cut positions or add the two stick ends.
Tracked only ways to be true, not ways to be false, for boolean expressions.
Used the wrong cost for a split (matrix chain cost is arr[i - 1] * arr[k] * arr[j]).

nodes.name: DP on squares
nodes.description: Count squares of 1s with dp[i][j] = 1 + min(top, left, top-left); the largest rectangle reuses the histogram method on each row.

facets.explain: Explains why the minimum of three neighbours limits the square ending at a cell.
facets.implement: Writes the recurrence and sums (or maximizes) as asked.

misconceptions.desc: Took the minimum of only two neighbours.
Returned the largest square where the count of all squares was asked, or the reverse.
